answer: This Sybil defense prices identity, not signatures. Every new agent must post a bond locked for months, so an attacker backing a thousand shells pays a thousand times that capital, not a thousand cheap keys. Stakes are public, letting the network read them like an atlas of who funds whom, and a degree threshold counts only edges backed by value. Tasks route through a mesh where two independent agents countersign each request, so self-signed edges earn nothing. Honest agents earn yield, so attack cost rises faster than reward and every vertex links to a real payer, not a river of empty names.
